title: What are the sides of the rectangle in a cylinder's net?
description: A cylinder has radius seven centimetres and height ten centimetres. The board unrolls its curved surface into a rectangle, finds the long side from the distance round the base, and adds the two circles. Keeko's doubt is that the long side is the diameter.
teaching_notes: One idea: the curved surface unrolls into a rectangle whose long side is the circumference of the base and whose short side is the height. Watch for students who use the diameter for the long side.

source: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Find the sides
video_script.why: The child finds the sides of the rectangle in a cylinder's net by asking what each side wraps round, because the long side goes once round the base and the short side is the height.
video_script.substitution: radius 7 cm, height 10 cm, pi as 22/7; long side 2 x 22/7 x 7 = 44 cm; short side 10 cm; two circles of radius 7 cm.
video_script.anchor: the cylinder of the book, its curved surface unrolled into a rectangle between two circles
video_script.wrong_answer: the long side is fourteen centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the diameter, two times seven, as the long side; the diameter goes straight across the circle but the paper goes all the way round, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The net is a rectangle forty four centimetres by ten centimetres, with two circles of radius seven centimetres

final_answer.value: A 44 cm by 10 cm rectangle with two circles of radius 7 cm
final_answer.spoken: a forty four centimetre by ten centimetre rectangle with two circles of radius seven centimetres

hold_back: A 44 cm by 10 cm rectangle with two circles of radius 7 cm
maths_rules: the curved surface unrolls into a rectangle; one side goes once round the base, the other is the height
long side = circumference = 2 x pi x r = 2 x 22/7 x 7 = 2 x 22 = 44 cm
top and bottom are two circles of radius 7 cm joined to the long side
wrong idea: the diameter 2 x 7 = 14 cm goes straight across the circle, not round it
video_script.design: One idea: ask what each side wraps round. The tube unrolls on the stage; the long side is traced round the base circle and the short side is traced up the height.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the long side is fourteen centimetres, because the diameter is two times seven.
<bookmark mark='across'/>The diameter goes straight across the circle. The paper goes all the way round.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The long side is the distance round the circle, which is much longer than fourteen.
